info.bio:
Sonny & Cher fueron un dúo musical conformado por el politico Sonny Bono y por la actriz y cantante Cher que cosecharon grandes éxitos entre 1963 y 1975, siendo también durante ese tiempo esposos y padres de Chastity Bono.

Historia 

El dúo nació cuando Cher conoció a Salvatore Phillip Bono en una conocida cafetería de Los Angeles, ella se enamoró a primera vista, y le convenció a él para que la dejará vivir en su casa. Él, divorciado

scenes.name: Pop protesta y folk rock (1965)
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: El pop quería profundidad y el folk quería fama. En 1963 Dylan condensó el miedo atómico en «A Hard Rain’s a-Gonna Fall» y Peter, Paul and Mary llevaron «Blowin’ in the Wind» al número 2; en 1964 los Searchers demostraron que una letra sobre lluvia radiactiva («What Have They Done to the Rain») podía entrar en el Top 20. En 1965 Dylan triunfó en Inglaterra, Donovan arrasó con «Catch the Wind» y el «Mr Tambourine Man» de los Byrds abrió la veda: todos versionaban a Dylan y la «Pop Protest» amenazaba con ser una moda. «Eve of Destruction», de P. F. Sloan cantada por Barry McGuire y prohibida por la BBC, fue su cénit comercial y su nadir artístico. Tom Wilson, productor despedido por Dylan, añadió instrumentos eléctricos a la versión acústica de «The Sound of Silence» de Simon & Garfunkel, primer número 1 estadounidense de 1966 y señal de que el mercado de masas no temería la profundidad.

scenes.name: Los Ángeles y el Sunset Strip
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: La ciudad que en 1966 se convirtió en la meca internacional del pop. Bobby Jameson, de veinte años, en los márgenes de la industria (había grabado canciones tempranas de Jagger/Richards en Londres y se presentó al casting de los Monkees), grabó con miembros de los Leaves y el primer batería de Love «Vietnam» (Mira, octubre de 1965): órgano de película de terror, ritmo Bo Diddley y un aullido sin esperanza, el blues de un hombre blanco, retirado casi al instante. Detenido por drogas tras su primer LSD con Danny Hutton, se libró del reclutamiento al confesarlo en el examen. La adolescente Jan Smithers, habitual de Malibú y del Strip, decía a Newsweek que a veces quería gritar y golpear la almohada.

scenes.name: Aberfan, Cathy Come Home y la Gran Bretaña olvidada
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: El 21 de octubre de 1966 una escombrera de carbón se desplomó sobre Aberfan, en los valles de Gales del Sur, y sepultó la escuela de Pantglas: murió la mitad de sus 240 alumnos. La cobertura televisiva arrancó la atención del país de la capital y sus riquezas hacia la gente y los lugares olvidados de una Gran Bretaña que ya no parecía tan grande. El 16 de noviembre la BBC emitió Cathy Come Home de Ken Loach, Tony Garnett y Jeremy Sandford (marido de Nell Dunn): mezcla de drama y documental sobre una pareja joven y moderna que cae hasta los albergues de Newington Lodge y pierde a sus hijos, «víctimas del Estado del bienestar». La vio una quinta parte del país; tres días después nació la organización Shelter.

podcast.title: Unofficial Marriage (1964)
podcast.body: Sonny and Cher were unofficially married in 1964 when Sonny was 29 and Cher was 18. "They were unofficially married in 1964 when Sunny was 29 and Share was 18."

podcast.title: Career Struggles (1971)
podcast.body: By 1971, six years after their hit "I Got You Babe," Sonny and Cher were in their fourth year without a record label and two years into their official marriage, fighting for the survival of their careers despite playing live shows. "Six years after I got you, babe, in 1971, Sunny and Share were in year four of being without a record label in two years into their official marriage."

podcast.title: Separation of Careers (1971)
podcast.body: Sonny worked to secure Cher a solo deal with Cap Records (later MCA). A condition of this deal was that Sonny, known for his controlling involvement in Cher's career, could not be involved in her solo work. "A stipulation in that deal though was that Sunny, who was known to be very controlling of Share's career, could not be involved in her solo career."

podcast.title: The Sonny & Cher Comedy Hour (1971-1974)
podcast.body: This variety show aired on CBS from August 1971 to May 29, 1974. Critic John Leonard praised its "inspired comic touch" and noted its "innocence," which resonated with the "weariness" felt in 1970s America. The show concluded when Sonny and Cher divorced in 1974. "The singers Sunny and Cher got their own show in 1971. It aired on CBS from August 1971 to May 29th, 1974."

podcast.title: Marriage and Career (Mid-60s to 1975)
podcast.body: Sonny and Cher were married in the mid-1960s and shared a successful career that included both recording and television appearances. Their professional partnership continued until their divorce in 1975. "Sonny and Cher were married in the mid-60s and shared a career that spanned records and television until they divorced in 1975."

podcast.title: Cher's Dissatisfaction with Era's Music (1977)
podcast.body: By 1977, Cher publicly stated her dislike for most of the music from the Sonny & Cher era, admitting she only genuinely liked two albums from that period. "In 1977, though Cher said she did not like the music from the Sunny and Cher era. There were only two albums of that era she said that she liked."

podcast.title: Late Night with David Letterman Reunion (1987)
podcast.body: On November 13, 1987, Sonny and Cher reunited on "Late Night with David Letterman," holding hands and singing their classic hit "I Got You Babe," an event that captivated audiences. "So I was watching late night with David Letterman on November 13, 1987, when Sunny and Share reunited, and then they held hands and they sang, I got you, babe, the very epitome of a pop song."

podcast.title: Sonny's Controlling Nature
podcast.body: Sonny Bono was widely documented as being very controlling, a dynamic perhaps influenced by the age gap when they met (he was 28, she was 16). Cher eventually outgrew this dynamic, even calling him "a watered downs van golly" in 1974, though she later credited him for launching her career after his death. "Now it has been well documented that Sunny was very controlling. He was 28 and she was 16 when they met."

podcast.title: Temporary End and Revival of Show
podcast.body: "The Sonny & Cher Comedy Hour" ended with their divorce in 1974 but was revived for a couple of years in 1976 and 1977, during which time Cher was married to Greg Allman. In the interim, both Sonny and Cher pursued individual variety shows. "Sunny and Cher revived their show for a couple of years in 1976 and 1977. That was when Cher was married to Greg Olman."

xref.body: Carol Kaye's session credits include playing with Nancy Sinatra, The Monkees, Ray Charles, Sonny & Cher, Glen Campbell, Neil Young, Frank Zappa, and Tina Turner, underscoring her broad influence and demand. She also played with Frank Black of the Pixies on his 2006 record "Fast Man Rader". "Nancy Sinatra, the monkeys, Ray Charles, Sonny and Cher, Glenn Campbell, Neil Young, Frank Zap, a Tina Turner."
